items.stem: A founder builds a trip-planning app. Her first model lists station names and the order of stations. A user asks how long a trip takes at 5 PM. What should she conclude?

options.text: The model is wrong and should be thrown out.
options.feedback: It answers route questions correctly. It is incomplete for timing.

options.text: The model lacks distance and delays, so it cannot answer.
options.feedback: A model answers only the questions its details cover. Timing needs two more details.

options.text: The answer is in the station names if users read closely.
options.feedback: Station names say nothing about time.

options.text: The model has too many details and needs trimming.
options.feedback: The model has only two details. This question needs two more.

items.stem: A map team adds the color of every train to the model. What is the effect on the question "Which train do I take?"

options.text: The model answers the question more accurately.
options.feedback: The answer depends on station names and the order of stations. Color adds neither.

options.text: The model grows and the question is answered no better.
options.feedback: Color does not help choose a route, so the extra detail adds work and no value.

options.text: The model can no longer answer the question.
options.feedback: Extra details do not break the answer. They add clutter.

items.stem: An app developer checks that the app sends the order to the server when a user taps Order. Which level is she working at?

options.text: Level 1, where the user taps Order.
options.feedback: The tap is what the user sees. The developer checks what the app does with it.

options.text: Level 3, where the server saves the order.
options.feedback: Saving happens after the server receives the order. The developer checks what leaves the app.

options.text: Level 4, where the disk stores the row.
options.feedback: Disk writes sit far below the app. They are the database administrator's level.

options.text: Level 2, where the app sends the order.
options.feedback: Checking what leaves the app is the app developer's level.

items.stem: A new team member wants to understand how payments work before touching any code. Which description helps most at the start?

options.text: The complete database design with every table and column.
options.feedback: A full design holds more detail than a beginner can use.

options.text: A list of every network message with its byte count.
options.feedback: Byte counts are the lowest level. They help later.

options.text: A short story of the whole flow, with detail added step by step.
options.feedback: A top-level view shows the whole flow and lets her zoom in on one step at a time.
